precepts.text: The Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, but the children of Esau succeeded them when they had destroyed them and dwelt in their stead, as Israel did in Canaan; but we left Canaanites alive and Esau killed them all out by the sword.
precepts.point: Then the sons of Seir the Horite who inhabited the land, with their own dukes, Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. Esau learned dukes from the Horites, took the title and the land, and Seir the Hamite land became Edom.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Esau left Canaan because his riches and cattle were too great for him and Jacob to dwell together, and the land did not belong to him. “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” But Genesis 14:6 had already shown that the Horites dwelt in Mount Seir. So what became of them?

Genesis 36 lists the dukes of Esau's sons, the high titles: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, Korah, Gatam and Amalek, all of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah. Remember these dukes, because they are all around today under various names like German, Israeli and Polish. Then comes a surprise: “These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,” “And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.” Seir the Horite was a Hamite, and the Horites had dukes first. That is where Esau learned about dukes: he got among them, took their title and took their land.

Deuteronomy tells how: “The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead”. The Horims are the Horites, the same Hamite people. The children of Esau intermingled with them, then conquered them by the sword and dwelt in their place. So when you read about Seir it means Edom, but originally it was the land of the Horites, the children of Ham.

Moses adds, “as Israel did unto the land of his possession, which the Lord gave unto them.” Israel did the same in Canaan, but we did not kill off all the Canaanites; they kept living there. Esau did not waste any time. He killed them all out of there. That is the robber nature of Edom from the beginning: take the land, take the title, and destroy the people who were there.

precepts.text: Esau destroyed the Horims from before them and dwells in their stead unto this day: the conquered cave dwellers became cave dwellers.
precepts.point: Then the sons of Seir the Horite who inhabited the land, with their own dukes, Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. Esau learned dukes from the Horites, took the title and the land, and Seir the Hamite land became Edom.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Moses says it a second time: “As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day”. Esau destroyed the Horims and lived in their stead, and he is still there unto this day.

The name tells the rest. The Horims, or Horites, get their name from the Hebrew word for a cave or a hole, which shows they were known as cave dwellers, troglodytes, living in the mountains of Seir. These Hamites lived in the caves first. Esau went in, conquered the cave dwellers and became a cave dweller himself. And what does Caucasian mean? Cave dweller. Edom became a cave dweller. People say the white man is not Esau. Well, then who is he? Japheth? The hell he is. He is far from Japheth.

Malachi shows God's view of it: “yet I loved Jacob,” “And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” Christian theologians say hated means preferred less, but that sounds just as bad; it means hate. The dragons of the wilderness are the Arabs, the Nabataeans, who later pushed much of Esau out of that land or intermarried with him. Mount Seir is called Petra today, meaning rock. Edom, rich in Canaan, became a poor cave dweller in Seir, saying, “We are impoverished,” but vowing to return and build the desolate places, and God calls them the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation forever.

Obadiah describes the same people in the last days: “thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”, the cave dweller, “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” The Greeks, the Romans, Spain, France, Russia, Britain and America all exalt the eagle, and all are Caucasian. Show us a powerful black nation today that came out of caves and exalts itself as the eagle. It fits one people: the Europeans, who took Seir from the Horites and dwell in their stead unto this day.

precepts.text: The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they dwelt in their stead.
precepts.point: The Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and they succeeded them and dwelt in their stead, as Deuteronomy records.

note.label: Genesis 36: The Generations of Esau, Who Is Edom

precepts.why:
“As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day”.

The sons of Seir the Horite inhabited the land first; the Lord destroyed the Horims from before the children of Esau, and Esau's children succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. That is how the land of Seir became the land of Edom.

precepts.text: The giants the people feared perished through their own foolishness, for the Lord chose them not.
precepts.point: The giants were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom and perished through their own foolishness. There are no giants today; stature and skill in war saved none of them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

precepts.why:
Ammon's land also was accounted a land of giants, the Zamzummims, “A people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the Lord destroyed them before them”. Baruch tells why they perished: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.”

The giants the people feared were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge. Stature and skill in war saved none of them; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom, and the Ammonites succeeded them and dwelt in their stead.

There are no giants today.

precepts.text: This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of thee; Rahab's melted heart is that word fulfilled.
precepts.point: Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.

note.label: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies

precepts.why:
“This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations that are under the whole heaven, who shall hear report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.” The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations, and Rahab is that word fulfilled: “as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you”.

They heard the report, and they trembled. All the inhabitants of the land fainted because of Israel, exactly as the Lord said they would.

precepts.text: We took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city; we left none to remain.
precepts.point: Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“For Joshua drew not his hand back, wherewith he stretched out the spear, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.” All the inhabitants means the children were put to death also. This was not new. At Sihon’s cities: “And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain”.

So the children’s song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures. The Lord’s love is toward the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Sihon would not let us pass, for the LORD thy God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand; go verse upon precept and you see the Most High in the midst of the battle.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: Jephthah said “Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast”. Moses tells why: “But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.” Go verse upon precept and you see the Most High in the midst of the battle. Sihon coming out to Jahaz was not his own idea; the Lord hardened his spirit so that Israel would possess the land of the Amorites. They came against Israel, Israel did nothing to them, and the Lord delivered them into Israel’s hand.

precepts.text: The LORD our God delivered him before us, and we took all his cities at that time; from Aroer even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us, because the Lord and his angels were in the midst of Israel.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
“so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.” Here is how: “And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people. And we took all his cities at that time”. “From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord our God delivered all unto us”.

There was not one city too strong, because the Lord and his angels were in the midst of Israel. That is how Israel got the land from Arnon even unto Jabbok: not by taking it from Moab or Ammon, but the Lord gave it in battle when Sihon came out against his people.

precepts.text: Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not; Israel never touched Ammon's land, which proves the king's claim false.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why: “Only unto the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not, nor unto any place of the river Jabbok, nor unto the cities in the mountains, nor unto whatsoever the Lord our God forbad us.” Israel never touched Ammon’s land, which proves the king’s claim false. Jephthah said “Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon”, and the record agrees: Israel possessed the coasts of the Amorites “from Arnon even unto Jabbok”, and stopped where the Lord forbad. The king of Ammon was claiming what was never his; Jephthah knew the book does not say that, and nobody could talk him out of it.

points: Israel compassed mount Seir many days, and the Lord said, ye have compassed this mountain long enough; turn you northward and pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir, the people called the white man today.
They shall be afraid of you: the Most High put fear upon Esau so they would not trouble Israel, because he did not want a war; take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore, and meddle not with them.
